subject.title: [Feature]: Feature request: Per-agent isolated browser instances with per-profile proxy support (concurrent execution)

question: Should OpenClaw add per-profile managed-browser proxy config plus per-agent/subagent default browser-profile binding, and what security/compatibility model governs proxy credentials, SSRF enforcement, profile selection, inheritance, and resource limits?
rationale: The requested feature adds public config/API surface and changes browser egress plus logged-in session isolation semantics, so automation cannot safely choose the product and security boundary from source inspection alone.

options.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
options.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for secret-safe proxy auth, explicit SSRF proxy trust, profile inheritance and override rules, resource limits, diagnostics, docs, and tests.

options.title: Keep current explicit workarounds
options.body: Decline first-class per-agent/per-profile config for now and document explicit profile selection, browser.extraArgs, remote CDP, and node-host patterns as the supported path.

options.title: Split into narrower canonicals
options.body: Move proxy egress to #60035 and browser ownership/inheritance to #85672, then close this umbrella only after maintainers link the canonical split.

recommendation.title: Approve a gated browser-profile design
recommendation.body: Add the feature only with a documented contract for secret-safe proxy auth, explicit SSRF proxy trust, profile inheritance and override rules, resource limits, diagnostics, docs, and tests.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent browser plugin and docs/config ownership makes this the best available routing target for the browser profile security/product decision.
